Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Budibase CVE-2026-48150: POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign with global builder/admin grant in body · [LLM] Budibase: API key minted via /api/global/self/api_key then /api/public/v1/roles/assign within 5m
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Budibase audit log: builder.global / admin.global granted to user by non-global caller · [LLM] Budibase: rapid bulk POSTs to /api/public/v1/roles/assign from single source
Budibase CVE-2026-48150: POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign with global builder/admin grant in body AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP POSTs to the vulnerable Budibase public-API role-assignment endpoint that carry `builder:true` or `admin:true` in the JSON body — the exact payload shape that triggers CVE-2026-48150 mass-assignment. Article-specific: the controller spreads `assignmentProps` straight into the SDK, so the body content is the high-fidelity tell. Rationale: Endpoint path (`/api/public/v1/roles/assign`), method (POST), and body keys (`"builder":true` / `"admin":true`) are taken verbatim from the article's PoC curl. Both URL-encoded and raw forms covered for reverse-proxy logs that record query strings differently. Defender KQL left empty — body inspection is not in DeviceNetworkEvents. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g39-332f-68p9
ATT&CKT1068 T1190 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate tenant admin promoting a new builder via the public API (filter by SourceUserName allow-list)
  • Budibase upgrade scripts replaying recorded admin requests against a staging tenant
  • Penetration test / red team exercise reproducing the PoC for the same advisory
  • Automation that grants global-builder to service accounts post-onboarding
Suppression filter
| where SourceUserName !in~ ("svc-budibase-onboard", "svc-budibase-scim") | where RequestClientApplication !has "BudibaseAdminConsole"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull SourceIP + SourceUserName, look up the calling identity in Budibase admin console. Confirm whether the caller had global-builder or global-admin BEFORE the request — if not, treat as confirmed exploit. 2) Contain: revoke the API key (`/api/global/self/api_key` rotate), unset `builder.global` / `admin.global` on every userId in the request body, force-logout all sessions for the caller and any granted users, block the SourceIP at the ingress. 3) Hunt: pivot on SourceIP and SourceUserName for the prior 30 days against all `/api/public/v1/*` calls; enumerate every user whose `builder.global` or `admin.global` is currently true and verify against your role-baseline; check audit logs for SCIM/OIDC config edits made by the granted accounts.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where Message has_any ("\"builder\":true", "\"admin\":true", "builder%22%3Atrue", "admin%22%3Atrue")
    or DeviceCustomString1 has_any ("\"builder\":true", "\"admin\":true")
    or DeviceCustomString2 has_any ("\"builder\":true", "\"admin\":true")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, RequestContext, Message, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Budibase Role-Assign Endpoint Hit with Global Privilege Grant
id: 8b2c4f9e-2a1d-4f6c-9a8b-7c5e6d4f3a2b
description: Detects HTTP POST to Budibase /api/public/v1/roles/assign carrying builder=true or admin=true in the body — CVE-2026-48150 mass-assignment payload
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/13
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1098
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: POST
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/api/public/v1/roles/assign'
  selection_body:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - '"builder":true'
      - '"admin":true'
      - 'builder%22%3Atrue'
      - 'admin%22%3Atrue'
  condition: selection and selection_body
level: high
@http.url_details.path:"/api/public/v1/roles/assign" @http.method:POST @http.status_code:[200 TO 299] ("builder\":true" OR "admin\":true" OR builder%22%3Atrue OR admin%22%3Atrue)
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agent values(Web.status) as status values(Web.uri_query) as uri_query from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/api/public/v1/roles/assign*" AND Web.http_method="POST" by Web.src, Web.user, Web.url, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search uri_query="*\"builder\":true*" OR uri_query="*\"admin\":true*" OR uri_query="*builder%22%3Atrue*" OR uri_query="*admin%22%3Atrue*" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agent values(Web.status) as status values(Web.uri_query) as uri_query from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/api/public/v1/roles/assign*" AND Web.http_method="POST" by Web.src, Web.user, Web.url, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | search uri_query="*\"builder\":true*" OR uri_query="*\"admin\":true*" OR uri_query="*builder%22%3Atrue*" OR uri_query="*admin%22%3Atrue*" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Budibase audit log: builder.global / admin.global granted to user by non-global caller AIActions on Objectives High
Parses Budibase server stdout / audit lines forwarded as Syslog for the role-assignment mutation introduced by CVE-2026-48150. Flags lines where the SDK wrote `builder.global=true` or `admin.global=true` on a user account, then extracts the target userId and grant scope so the analyst can correlate with the caller identity. Rationale: Audit-log strings (`/api/public/v1/roles/assign`, `builder.global`, `admin.global`, `x-budibase-api-key`, `us_` userId prefix, `app_` appId prefix) all come straight from the article's controller/SDK code paths and PoC curl. Sentinel `extend` columns are created from the raw `SyslogMessage`, not referenced as table columns. Defender KQL left blank — Budibase audit logs do not ship to Defender XDR tables. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh
ATT&CKT1098 T1068
Data sourcesChange.Account_Management
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Tenant admin doing legitimate role assignment via the public API (caller will already be global-admin)
  • Budibase Enterprise migration scripts seeding role state on a fresh install
  • Internal IaC / provisioning workflow that grants global-builder to a CI service account
Suppression filter
| where CallerApiKey !in ("<known-svc-key-hash1>", "<known-svc-key-hash2>")
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract `TargetUserId` and `CallerApiKey` from the alert. Look up the caller's role state at T-5min in Budibase admin — if `builder.global=false` and `admin.global=false` with `builder.apps` set, exploit is confirmed. 2) Contain: revoke caller's API key, reset target user's role to the baseline (re-apply `builder.apps` scope, unset `global`), force-logout all granted users. 3) Hunt: search Syslog for any other `roles/assign` writes by the same `CallerApiKey` or `AppIdHeader` in the prior 30 days; pivot on `TargetUserId` to find any SCIM / OIDC / datasource changes those users made post-grant.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("budibase", "node", "budibase-worker", "budibase-apps")
| where SyslogMessage has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("\"builder\":true", "\"admin\":true", "builder.global", "admin.global")
| extend TargetUserId = extract(@"us_[a-z0-9]+", 0, SyslogMessage)
| extend GrantedScope = case(
    SyslogMessage has "admin.global" or SyslogMessage has "\"admin\":true", "admin.global",
    SyslogMessage has "builder.global" or SyslogMessage has "\"builder\":true", "builder.global",
    "unknown")
| extend CallerApiKey = extract(@"x-budibase-api-key[^a-f0-9]*([a-f0-9]{16,})", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend AppIdHeader = extract(@"app_[a-z0-9]+", 0, SyslogMessage)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, GrantedScope, TargetUserId, CallerApiKey, AppIdHeader, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(nodejs OR docker) "/api/public/v1/roles/assign" ("builder.global" OR "admin.global" OR "builder\":true" OR "admin\":true") @service:budibase*
APPLICATION

Budibase: rapid bulk POSTs to /api/public/v1/roles/assign from single source AIActions on Objectives Medium
Catches mass-assignment abuse where an attacker sweeps multiple users (or repeatedly flips builder→admin on themselves, per article PoC step 4) via repeated calls to the vulnerable endpoint. Threshold tuned to the article's pattern where Alice issued one grant-builder + one grant-admin in quick succession. Rationale: Article's PoC shows two consecutive grants from one identity (Alice→victim, then Alice→Alice). A workspace-scoped builder making >3 POSTs to this endpoint in 5 minutes has no legitimate use case — the public API is not normally driven from manual operator workflows. Threshold > 3 over 5m chosen to catch the PoC pattern while tolerating one legitimate scripted promotion. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh
ATT&CKT1068 T1098
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SCIM bulk-sync after IdP group change replays many role assignments
  • Tenant migration / IaC apply that grants role to many users at once
  • Budibase Enterprise onboarding script seeding builders for a new workspace
  • Load-test or CI smoke test against staging tenant
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("<scim-svc-ip>", "<ci-svc-ip>")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate every userId in the bursting calls' bodies — these are the privilege grant targets. Cross-reference SourceIP against known CI / SCIM service ranges. 2) Contain: revoke the caller's API key; for every targeted userId run the inverse SDK call to unset `builder.global` / `admin.global` and restore `builder.apps` scope. 3) Hunt: pivot on the SourceIP and SourceUserName for the prior 30 days to find recon (`GET /api/global/users`) or earlier suspicious public-API usage; check whether any newly-elevated users created datasources / automations / SCIM-OIDC config changes after the burst.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where RequestURL has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| summarize PostCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            DistinctBodies = dcount(Message),
            DistinctUserAgents = dcount(RequestClientApplication),
            SampleBody = any(Message)
            by SourceIP, SourceUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where PostCount > 3
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by PostCount desc

Budibase: API key minted via /api/global/self/api_key then /api/public/v1/roles/assign within 5m AIExploitation High
Reproduces the exact two-step chain from the CVE-2026-48150 PoC (step 2 mints the key, step 3 uses it to escalate). Joining the mint event to the assign event narrows on attacker tradecraft — the legitimate operator path uses long-lived keys, not key-minted-then-used. Rationale: Two-step chain (`GET /api/global/self/api_key` → `POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign`) is the exact tradecraft documented in the PoC (steps 2 and 3). 5-minute window matches the human-operator pace shown in the article and rules out long-lived legitimate keys. Datadog query is OR-joined for use as a rule-level correlation; not a single search-bar match. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xp4-cf37-ppjh
ATT&CKT1098.001 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator setting up new automation pulls a self-key then immediately tests it against the public API
  • Internal onboarding tooling that scripts both calls back-to-back for new builders
  • Pen test / red team validating CVE-2026-48150 against a tenant
Suppression filter
| where SourceUserName !in~ ("svc-budibase-onboard", "svc-budibase-ci")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the caller from the join, verify whether they already had global-builder/global-admin before `KeyMintTime` — if not, this is the CVE chain. 2) Contain: revoke the minted API key, unset elevated flags on every userId named in the assign request body, force-logout the caller and granted users. 3) Hunt: scan the prior 30 days for the same SourceIP/SourceUserName hitting `/api/global/self/api_key`; pivot on the minted key prefix in subsequent public-API calls to find post-escalation reconnaissance or datasource credential reads.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 5;
let KeyMints = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has "/api/global/self/api_key"
    | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
    | project KeyMintTime = TimeGenerated, MintSourceIP = SourceIP, MintSourceUser = SourceUserName, MintUA = RequestClientApplication;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RequestURL has "/api/public/v1/roles/assign"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| join kind=inner KeyMints on $left.SourceIP == $right.MintSourceIP
| where TimeGenerated between (KeyMintTime .. KeyMintTime + WindowMinutes * 1m)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, KeyMintTime)
| project KeyMintTime, AssignTime = TimeGenerated, DelaySec, SourceIP, SourceUserName, MintSourceUser, MintUA, AssignUA = RequestClientApplication, RequestURL, RequestMethod, Message
| order by AssignTime desc
(@http.url_details.path:"/api/global/self/api_key" @http.method:GET) OR (@http.url_details.path:"/api/public/v1/roles/assign" @http.method:POST)

China-Linked Hackers Backdoored Linux Login Software to Hide for Nearly a Decade

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 11 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Instead of hiding on the laptops and servers defenders watch most closely, a China-nexus group spent close to a decade hidden inside the Linux login system itself. Sygnia, which tracks the group as Velvet Ant, says it backdoored the PAM and OpenSSH components that decide who is allowed to sign in, planting its access where ordinary cleanup could not reach it. The network it targeted had no

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Internet-facing web service spawning interactive SSH into management subnet · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Unauthorized write to Linux PAM authentication module (pam_unix.so swap) · [LLM] Unauthorized modification of OpenSSH sshd or ssh client binary · [LLM] First-seen pam_unix.so / sshd / ssh binary hash in Linux fleet
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] sshd writing to non-standard files (credential-capture log artifact) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Unauthorized write to Linux PAM authentication module (pam_unix.so swap) AIInstallation High
Detects file creation/modification of pam_unix.so (or sibling PAM modules) by any process other than the system package manager. Velvet Ant's Operation Highland replaced this exact module with 9 backdoored builds that accepted a magic password and logged real credentials — direct swap is the highest-fidelity persistence pivot in the campaign. Rationale: Article + Sygnia blog explicitly name pam_unix.so as the swapped module with 9 backdoored variants discovered. File-write to canonical PAM module paths by a non-package-manager process is a direct hit on the documented TTP and effectively unfalsifiable without legitimate package activity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/operation-highland-velvet-ant/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/china-nexus-group-hid-in-linux-login-system-for-nearly-a-decade
ATT&CKT1556.003 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Distro security update outside the maintained package-manager allowlist (e.g. manually invoked 'install' on a downloaded .deb via curl|sh)
  • Configuration management agent (Ansible/Salt/Puppet) deploying a custom or in-house PAM module under a non-standard process name
  • Container-image build process writing PAM modules during image construction
  • System administrator manually reinstalling pam package via 'apt-get install --reinstall' under sudo from interactive shell
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ansible","salt-minion","puppet","chef-client","cfengine") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--reinstall","makepkg","rpmbuild"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — extract SHA256 of the written .so; compare against distro package hash via 'rpm -V pam' or 'dpkg --verify libpam-modules'; review process tree of InitiatingProcessFileName and its parent; check whether the host had a sanctioned change window. 2) Contain — isolate the host; snapshot /lib*/security/ and /etc/pam.d/ for forensics; revoke and rotate every credential used to SSH to or sudo on the host within the lookback (article: credentials captured at login). 3) Hunt — fan out the SHA256 across the Linux fleet; pull sshd and ssh binary hashes from the same host; hunt outbound DNS/TCP from sshd-context processes for any kill-switch beacon.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"/lib/security/", @"/lib64/security/", @"/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/", @"/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/", @"/usr/lib64/security/")
| where FileName startswith "pam_" and FileName endswith ".so"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","dpkg-deb","apt","apt-get","aptitude","unattended-upgrade","yum","dnf","rpm","zypper","pacman","ldconfig","snapd","snap")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, MD5, PreviousFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/lib/security/","/lib64/security/","/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/","/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/security/","/usr/lib64/security/")
| where TargetFileName startswith "pam_" and TargetFileName endswith ".so"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("dpkg","dpkg-deb","apt","apt-get","aptitude","unattended-upgrade","yum","dnf","rpm","zypper","pacman","ldconfig","snapd","snap")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unauthorized modification of OpenSSH sshd or ssh client binary AIInstallation High
Detects write or replacement of the canonical OpenSSH binaries (/usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/ssh) outside of package-manager updates. Operation Highland modified these binaries to log credentials and every command typed with a hidden switch to silence logging, making any uncontrolled write to them campaign-defining. Rationale: Article + Sygnia state sshd/ssh were altered to log credentials and typed commands with a hidden disable switch. Detecting file writes to the canonical OpenSSH paths by anything other than the package manager is a direct, low-FP hit on the documented persistence method. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/operation-highland-velvet-ant/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/china-nexus-group-hid-in-linux-login-system-for-nearly-a-decade
ATT&CKT1554 T1556 T1056.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • openssh-server package upgrade run through a wrapper (e.g. unattended-upgrade not present, security-update.sh script invokes apt)
  • Hardened-build pipeline replacing distro openssh with an internally compiled binary deployed via Ansible/Salt
  • Container image bake writing sshd into a layer at build time
  • Manual 'apt-get install --reinstall openssh-server' by a sysadmin under interactive sudo
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ansible","salt-minion","puppet","chef-client","cfengine") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--reinstall"
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull SHA256 of new sshd/ssh; compare to distro package hash ('dpkg-query -W -f=' then 'apt-cache' or 'rpm -qf'); check for a hidden config flag (e.g. extra env var or stat-suppressed sibling file) and grep strings for unexpected log paths. 2) Contain — isolate host; capture binary + memory; restore sshd from a verified distro mirror; kill all active sshd sessions; force rotation of every SSH credential used against the host plus any key material loaded by users that logged in since modification. 3) Hunt — fleet-wide hash search for the same SHA256 on sshd, ssh, ssh-keygen, scp, sftp; cross-check pam_unix.so on the same host (Velvet Ant typically modifies both); review auth log gaps and any sshd outbound connections.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath in~ ("/usr/sbin/","/usr/bin/")
| where FileName in~ ("sshd","ssh","ssh-keygen","scp","sftp","ssh-agent")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","dpkg-deb","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","yum","dnf","rpm","zypper","pacman","snapd","snap")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, MD5, PreviousFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath in~ ("/usr/sbin/sshd","/usr/bin/sshd","/usr/bin/ssh","/usr/sbin/ssh","/usr/bin/ssh-keygen","/usr/bin/scp","/usr/bin/sftp","/usr/bin/ssh-agent")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("dpkg","dpkg-deb","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","yum","dnf","rpm","zypper","pacman","snapd","snap")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

      - '/pacman'
      - '/snapd'
  condition: selection and not filter_pkgmgr
falsepositives:
  - openssh-server package upgrade via a non-allowlisted wrapper
  - In-house compiled OpenSSH deployed by configuration management
level: high

| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(dpkg|dpkg-deb|apt|apt-get|unattended-upgrade|yum|dnf|rpm|zypper|pacman|snapd)$/i

sshd writing to non-standard files (credential-capture log artifact) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the sshd process writing to file paths outside its expected runtime set (PID file, audit/syslog sockets, sftp transfer targets). The Operation Highland sshd backdoor recorded every credential and typed command to a hidden file; any file-write originating from sshd to /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /etc, or a non-standard path under /var is the artefact. Rationale: Article: Operation Highland sshd 'logging credentials and every command typed, with a hidden switch to turn that logging off when needed.' The capture file has to land somewhere on disk. sshd's expected write set is small (PID, syslog forwards, user .ssh, sftp transfers) — anything else from sshd is a credential-capture candidate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/operation-highland-velvet-ant/
ATT&CKT1056.001 T1003.008 T1556.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • sftp-internal subsystem inside sshd writing user-uploaded files to non-/home destinations
  • PAM session module writing motd/lastlog timestamps via sshd context to a vendor-custom path
  • Container-friendly sshd builds that write a runtime socket to /tmp under a non-standard name
  • Custom sshd ChrootDirectory configurations placing user data outside /home
  • Local PAM module from an EDR/UEBA agent writing audit breadcrumbs into /var/lib/<vendor>/
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/var/lib/" and FolderPath has_any ("crowdstrike","sentinelone","defender","qualys","rapid7"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — read the written file (cat / xxd first bytes) to confirm credential-style content (usernames, plaintext passwords, typed commands); cross-check sshd binary SHA256 against the distro package. 2) Contain — isolate host; copy and quarantine the capture file for forensics; replace sshd from verified package source; force password + key rotation for every account that authenticated to the host since the file's first-seen timestamp. 3) Hunt — pivot on the file path across the Linux fleet; check for matching pam_unix.so anomalies; review egress from sshd-context to identify out-of-band exfil of the capture file.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sshd"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("/usr/sbin/","/usr/bin/")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where not (FolderPath in~ ("/var/run/","/run/","/var/log/","/var/empty/sshd/","/var/lib/sss/") )
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/home/" and FolderPath contains "/.ssh/")
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/root/.ssh/")
| where not (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/ssh-")
| where FileName !in~ ("sshd.pid","auth.log","secure","lastlog","wtmp","btmp","utmp")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName =~ "sshd"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where not (TargetFilePath startswith "/var/run/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/run/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/log/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/empty/sshd/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/lib/sss/")
| where not (TargetFilePath startswith "/home/" and TargetFilePath contains "/.ssh/")
| where not (TargetFilePath startswith "/root/.ssh/")
| where not (TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/ssh-")
| where TargetFileName !in~ ("sshd.pid","auth.log","secure","lastlog","wtmp","btmp","utmp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Internet-facing web service spawning interactive SSH into management subnet AIDelivery High
Detects a web server process (httpd, nginx, apache2, tomcat, php-fpm, node, java app server) spawning ssh/scp/sftp/sshpass to an internal RFC1918 destination — the exact pivot Sygnia attributes to Operation Highland, where an internet-facing web server was used as a bridge to open remote sessions deep inside an air-gapped segment. Rationale: Article: 'used other disguised tools and an internet-facing web server as a bridge, passing commands through it to open remote sessions deep inside the segment that had no direct internet access.' A web-server parent spawning ssh/scp/sftp/socat at all is rare in production; targeting RFC1918 makes it the pivot signature. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/operation-highland-velvet-ant/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/china-nexus-group-hid-in-linux-login-system-for-nearly-a-decade
ATT&CKT1190 T1133 T1021.004 T1090.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI/CD agent embedded in a web tier (e.g. Jenkins runner under tomcat) legitimately scp-ing build artefacts to internal hosts
  • Deploy hook in a PHP app calling 'ssh deploy@internal' as part of release automation
  • Healthcheck plugin shelling 'nc -zv internal-db 5432' from haproxy
  • Log-shipping script invoked from nginx error handler that uses scp to push debug bundles
  • Backup wrapper inside a java app server initiating scp to an internal backup target
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("jenkins","deploy","gitlab-runner","awx","rundeck") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("deploy","backup","rsync")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the web server access log for the same minute and identify the request path that triggered the spawn (webshell signature); inspect the SSH destination IP and the credential/key used; check whether the web server has a documented automation parent. 2) Contain — kill active ssh/socat session; block egress from web tier to management subnet at host firewall; quarantine any webshell artefact found in the web root; rotate keys/passwords for the target account. 3) Hunt — fan-out same parent→child pairing across other internet-facing hosts; pivot on the destination internal IP to identify what the attacker reached; check the destination for pam_unix.so / sshd hash anomalies.
let WebParents = dynamic(["httpd","nginx","apache2","tomcat","java","node","php-fpm","php-cgi","uwsgi","gunicorn","caddy","lighttpd","haproxy"]);
let PivotTools = dynamic(["ssh","sshpass","scp","sftp","plink","autossh","socat","ncat","nc"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebParents)
| where FileName in~ (PivotTools)
| extend RfcTarget = extract(@"(?:^|\s)(?:-[a-zA-Z]\s+)?(?:[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+@)?((?:10\.|172\.(?:1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|192\.168\.)\d+\.\d+\.\d+|(?:10\.|172\.(?:1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|192\.168\.)[0-9.]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(RfcTarget) or ProcessCommandLine has_any (".internal",".corp",".local",".lan",".intranet")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, RfcTarget, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebParents = dynamic(["httpd","nginx","apache2","tomcat","java","node","php-fpm","php-cgi","uwsgi","gunicorn","caddy","lighttpd","haproxy"]);
let PivotTools = dynamic(["ssh","sshpass","scp","sftp","plink","autossh","socat","ncat","nc"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ (WebParents)
| where ActingProcessName in~ (PivotTools)
| extend RfcTarget = extract(@"(?:^|\s)(?:-[a-zA-Z]\s+)?(?:[A-Za-z0-9_\-]+@)?((?:10\.|172\.(?:1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|192\.168\.)[0-9.]+)", 1, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(RfcTarget) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".internal",".corp",".local",".lan",".intranet")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RfcTarget
| order by TimeGenerated desc

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.name:(httpd OR nginx OR apache2 OR tomcat OR java OR node OR php-fpm OR php-cgi OR uwsgi OR gunicorn OR caddy OR lighttpd OR haproxy) @process.name:(ssh OR sshpass OR scp OR sftp OR plink OR autossh OR socat OR ncat OR nc) (@process.command_line:*10.* OR @process.command_line:*172.16.* OR @process.command_line:*172.17.* OR @process.command_line:*172.18.* OR @process.command_line:*172.19.* OR @process.command_line:*172.2* OR @process.command_line:*172.30.* OR @process.command_line:*172.31.* OR @process.command_line:*192.168.* OR @process.command_line:*.internal* OR @process.command_line:*.corp* OR @process.command_line:*.local* OR @process.command_line:*.lan*)

| regex("(10\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\.|192\\.168\\.|\\.internal|\\.corp|\\.local|\\.lan|\\.intranet)", field=CommandLine)

First-seen pam_unix.so / sshd / ssh binary hash in Linux fleet AIInstallation Medium
Anti-baseline hunting query: surfaces SHA256 values of pam_unix.so, sshd, ssh, scp, sftp that appear in the recent window but were never observed in the 60-day baseline. Velvet Ant built 9 distinct compile-variants of pam_unix.so per host — a fresh hash on a long-stable binary is the canonical indicator regardless of how it got there. Rationale: Article + Sygnia: 9 distinct compile-variants of pam_unix.so per Operation Highland host. Hash-anti-baseline catches the variant regardless of write path; works even when the swap predates monitoring (because the new hash will eventually appear in execution/load telemetry). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sygnia.co/blog/operation-highland-velvet-ant/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/china-nexus-group-hid-in-linux-login-system-for-nearly-a-decade
ATT&CKT1554 T1556.003 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Distro security update introducing a new openssh-server build (legitimate new hash, fleet-wide)
  • Newly onboarded host running a different distro version not present in baseline
  • libpam-modules upgrade pushing a new pam_unix.so build
  • In-house custom-compiled OpenSSH rollout under a change ticket
  • Hardened-image refresh from golden image producing new but legitimate hashes
Suppression filter
| where not (FirstSeen > ago(48h) and HostCount > 100)
Response runbook
1) Triage — correlate the new hash against the package metadata on the host ('rpm -V', 'dpkg -V libpam-modules openssh-server') and against the distro vendor's signed package hash; if the hash is unaccounted for, treat as suspect. 2) Contain — isolate the host; preserve binary + memory; restore from verified package mirror; rotate credentials used since the binary first appeared. 3) Hunt — pivot on the unaccounted hash across the fleet to find all infected hosts; cross-check whether the same hosts also have anomalous sshd or pam_unix.so; review egress from those hosts during their first-seen window.
let Lookback = 60d;
let Recent = 7d;
let AuthBinaries = dynamic(["sshd","ssh","scp","sftp","ssh-keygen","ssh-agent"]);
let BaselineExec = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where FileName in~ (AuthBinaries) and FolderPath in~ ("/usr/sbin/","/usr/bin/")
    | summarize by SHA256, FileName;
let RecentExec = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Recent)
    | where FileName in~ (AuthBinaries) and FolderPath in~ ("/usr/sbin/","/usr/bin/")
    | summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), HostCount = dcount(DeviceId), AnyHost = any(DeviceName), AnyCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine) by SHA256, FileName, FolderPath;
let NewExec = RecentExec | join kind=leftanti BaselineExec on SHA256, FileName | extend Kind = "sshd/ssh exec";
let BaselineLoad = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where FileName == "pam_unix.so"
    | summarize by SHA256, FileName;
let RecentLoad = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Recent)
    | where FileName == "pam_unix.so"
    | summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), HostCount = dcount(DeviceId), AnyHost = any(DeviceName), AnyCmd = "" by SHA256, FileName, FolderPath;
let NewLoad = RecentLoad | join kind=leftanti BaselineLoad on SHA256, FileName | extend Kind = "pam_unix.so load";
union NewExec, NewLoad
| order by FirstSeen desc
let Lookback = 60d;
let Recent = 7d;
let AuthBinaries = dynamic(["sshd","ssh","scp","sftp","ssh-keygen","ssh-agent"]);
let Baseline = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where ActingProcessName in~ (AuthBinaries)
    | summarize by Hash = tostring(SHA256), ActingProcessName;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Recent)
| where ActingProcessName in~ (AuthBinaries)
| extend Hash = tostring(SHA256)
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on Hash, ActingProcessName
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), HostCount = dcount(DvcHostname), AnyHost = any(DvcHostname), AnyCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine) by Hash, ActingProcessName
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(/usr/sbin/sshd OR /usr/bin/sshd OR /usr/bin/ssh OR /usr/sbin/ssh OR /usr/bin/scp OR /usr/bin/sftp OR /usr/bin/ssh-keygen OR /usr/bin/ssh-agent) @process.executable.hash:*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(usr\/sbin\/sshd|usr\/bin\/sshd|usr\/bin\/ssh|usr\/sbin\/ssh|usr\/bin\/scp|usr\/bin\/sftp|usr\/bin\/ssh-keygen|usr\/bin\/ssh-agent)$/i
| groupBy([SHA256HashData, ImageFileName], function={ min(_time, as=FirstSeen) | count(field=aid, distinct=true, as=HostCount) })
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(usr\/sbin\/sshd|usr\/bin\/sshd|usr\/bin\/ssh|usr\/sbin\/ssh|usr\/bin\/scp|usr\/bin\/sftp|usr\/bin\/ssh-keygen|usr\/bin\/ssh-agent)$/i _time<now()-7d | groupBy([SHA256HashData], function=count(as=BaselineCount))}, field=SHA256HashData, include=[BaselineCount], mode=left)
| BaselineCount=null
| sort(FirstSeen, order=desc)
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.dest) as hosts from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("sshd","ssh","scp","sftp") earliest=-60d@d latest=-7d@d by Processes.process_hash Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process_hash as baseline_hash | append [ | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as recent_firstTime max(_time) as recent_lastTime values(Processes.dest) as recent_hosts from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("sshd","ssh","scp","sftp") earliest=-7d@d by Processes.process_hash Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process_hash as recent_hash ] | stats values(*) as * by recent_hash | where isnotnull(recent_hash) AND isnull(baseline_hash)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.dest) as hosts from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("sshd","ssh","scp","sftp") earliest=-60d@d latest=-7d@d by Processes.process_hash Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process_hash as baseline_hash | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as recent_firstTime max(_time) as recent_lastTime values(Processes.dest) as recent_hosts from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("sshd","ssh","scp","sftp") earliest=-7d@d by Processes.process_hash Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process_hash as recent_hash ] | stats values(*) as * by recent_hash | where isnotnull(recent_hash) AND isnull(baseline_hash)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Agentjacking Attack Tricks AI Coding Agents Into Running Malicious Code

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 11 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have described what they say is a new class of attack that can trick artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents into running arbitrary code on developer machines. Called Agentjacking by Tenet Security, the attack can be triggered by means of a fake error report crafted using Sentry, an open-source error-tracking and performance-monitoring platform. "The attack

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) spawning shell that fetch-and-executes remote payload
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Agentjacking C2/exfiltration to advisory-tracker.com (Tenet Sentry-MCP attack) · [LLM] AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials / env (Agentjacking credential access) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Agentjacking C2/exfiltration to advisory-tracker.com (Tenet Sentry-MCP attack) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Tenet Security 'Agentjacking' exfiltration endpoint that receives developer environment variables, git credentials, repo URLs and tokens stolen by npm typosquat packages that a hijacked AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) was tricked into installing via a forged Sentry issue. Both DNS resolution and TCP egress are pivoted because the npm-installed payload posts to https://advisory-tracker.com/api/v1/telemetry. Rationale: advisory-tracker.com and 52.206.47.180 are the Tenet-published exfiltration endpoint for the Agentjacking PoC, also enumerated in the PSPDFKit IOC repo for the related Sentry npm typosquat campaign. Cross-checked: Tenet's blog post and the PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs GitHub repo both list the same domain + IP + /api/v1/telemetry path, so the IOC has independent corroboration beyond the THN article. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/agentjacking-attacks-hijack-ai/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised purple-team replay of the Tenet PoC from a research VM
  • Security-research sandbox detonating one of the IOC-listed npm packages
  • Threat-intel enrichment platform (VirusTotal/urlscan) auto-resolving advisory-tracker.com from a SOC analyst workstation
  • DNS-passive-replication sensor logging the domain without an actual host connecting
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\sandbox\", @"\detonation\", @"\threat-research\")) and not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("vt-cli.exe","urlscan.exe","virustotal.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceProcessEvents for the same DeviceId in the 10 min before the connection, walk the process tree (claude.exe / cursor.exe / code.exe → node.exe → npm/npx → outbound), and confirm the developer was using an AI coding agent against Sentry. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response; immediately rotate every credential exposed in env on a developer box — git PAT, npm _authToken, AWS/GCP keys, .env secrets, Sentry DSN, any cloud-CLI session token. Quarantine the npm cache and node_modules under the suspect project. 3) Hunt: enumerate every host in the org that resolved advisory-tracker.com or hit 52.206.47.180 in the last 30 days; scan all developer repos for the typosquat package family in package-lock.json / yarn.lock; audit Sentry org membership against affected developers to find the injected issue ID.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "advisory-tracker.com" or RemoteIP == "52.206.47.180"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has "advisory-tracker.com" or DstIpAddr == "52.206.47.180"
    | extend Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImNetworkSession", Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator, Url),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has "advisory-tracker.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=SrcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery, Url=DnsQuery),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has "advisory-tracker.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, User=tostring(""), Indicator=Name, Url=Name)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 4e3f8d9a-2b1c-4f5e-9d0a-6c7e1f8b2a3d
status: experimental
description: DNS query for advisory-tracker.com, the Tenet 'Agentjacking' exfiltration endpoint receiving developer credentials, environment variables and git tokens posted by npm typosquats installed by a hijacked AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) after a forged Sentry issue.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/agentjacking-attack-tricks-ai-coding.html
  - https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/

date: 2026/06/12

detection:

level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) AND ((@EventID:3 AND (@DestinationHostname:*advisory-tracker.com OR @DestinationIp:52.206.47.180)) OR (@EventID:22 AND @QueryName:*advisory-tracker.com) OR @network.destination.ip:52.206.47.180)

NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) spawning shell that fetch-and-executes remote payload AIInstallation High
Hunts the Agentjacking execution stage: after a forged Sentry MCP event is rendered as 'Resolution' guidance, the AI coding agent runs the attacker's instruction on the developer's machine. Specifically targets the Claude / Cursor / Codex process tree spawning cmd/PowerShell/bash/node that downloads-and-evaluates remote content (curl|sh, IEX DownloadString, node -e fetch, base64-decoded shell) or directly references the Tenet exfil host. Rationale: Article + Tenet blog both describe AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) reading a forged Sentry 'Resolution' over MCP and executing the attacker's shell command on the developer machine with developer privileges. Anchors on the article-specific parent-process names plus the standard fetch-and-execute payload shapes attacker injections use, and includes the corroborated advisory-tracker.com host so a literal reference fires high-confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.007 T1105 T1204
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer asking the agent to run a legitimate install one-liner from a vendor (e.g. nvm, rustup, ohmyzsh) that uses curl|bash
  • Agent-invoked build step that legitimately uses 'node -e' for codegen
  • PowerShell profile auto-load triggering Invoke-Expression on a vetted helper module
  • Security team running a Tenet PoC replay in a research VM
  • Internal devtools-team approved bootstrap scripts piped through bash
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh","sh.rustup.rs","get.docker.com","raw.githubusercontent.com/ohmyzsh","get-poetry.org")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\purple-team\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full parent chain (AI agent → shell → payload), the exact ProcessCommandLine, and any URL it pulled. Pull Sentry MCP request logs for that developer's session to identify the malicious issue ID; correlate to inbound POSTs to /api/0/store/ or /api/0/envelope/ on Sentry. 2) Contain: kill the descendant tree via Live Response; suspend the developer's AI-agent session; revoke every credential touchable from that shell context (git PAT, npm _authToken, AWS/GCP CLI tokens, SSH keys); quarantine downloaded artefacts and any new node_modules. 3) Hunt: pivot on the fetched URL, npm package name, and command hash across the dev fleet; query Sentry to see if the same injected issue body appears in other projects; audit which developers asked the agent to 'fix Sentry issues' in the last 14 days and verify their machines.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe"))
    or (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
        and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd"))
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-Expression","IEX(","IEX (","DownloadString","Net.WebClient","| sh","| bash","|sh ","|bash ","node -e","base64 -d","bash -c","powershell -enc","powershell -e ","powershell -EncodedCommand","curl -s ","wget -qO","advisory-tracker.com")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandparentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
     or (ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude","cursor","codex"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-Expression","IEX(","IEX (","DownloadString","Net.WebClient","| sh","| bash","|sh ","|bash ","node -e","base64 -d","bash -c","powershell -enc","powershell -EncodedCommand","curl -s","wget -qO","advisory-tracker.com")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe") OR Processes.process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("claude.exe","Claude.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")) AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe") by _time, Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(Invoke-Expression|IEX\s*\(|DownloadString|Net\.WebClient|curl\s+[^|]+\|\s*(sh|bash)|wget\s+-O\s*-|node\s+-e|base64\s+-d\s*\|\s*(sh|bash)|bash\s+-c\s+\$\(|powershell\s+-(e|enc|c)\s|advisory-tracker)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials / env (Agentjacking credential access) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Agentjacking credential_access stage where the hijacked AI agent's child process dumps environment variables and reads developer secret files — the specific data Tenet showed exfiltrated (env vars, git credentials, private repo URLs, AWS/cloud keys, npm _authToken, .env contents). Independent of the exfil IOC so it survives C2 rotation. Rationale: Tenet's writeup explicitly names the exfiltrated data classes — environment variables, Git credentials, private repository URLs, developer identities — which directly map to the file/env paths in this query. By anchoring on AI-coding-agent parents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) reading these specific resources, the detection survives even if the attacker rotates the advisory-tracker.com IOC. SENTRY_DSN is included because that's the bootstrap secret a typosquat would harvest first. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/agentjacking-attacks-hijack-ai/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately asking Claude/Cursor to debug a git auth failure (printenv / git config --get)
  • AI agent reading .npmrc _authToken to scope a sanctioned npm install
  • aws-cli / gcloud-cli config inspection invoked at developer request
  • ohmyzsh / shell-init scripts that printenv on session start under an agent terminal
  • CI emulator running inside Cursor terminal that dumps env for build context
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git config --global credential.helper","git config --get user.email","aws configure list","gcloud auth list")) and not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--debug-auth")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm parent chain (Claude/Cursor/Codex/node → shell → cred read) and verify the command-line wasn't a developer-issued debug step. Pull the Sentry MCP tool-call history for the developer's session and locate the issue body whose 'Resolution' text seeded the command. 2) Contain: rotate every credential whose file or env-var was read — git PAT, AWS/GCP CLI keys, SSH private keys, .env secrets, npm _authToken, the Sentry DSN itself. Force the developer to re-auth into all coding sessions and invalidate the host's OS keyring. 3) Hunt: across the dev fleet, find every AI-agent descendant that read the same credential paths in the last 30 days; correlate against outbound traffic from the same process tree to advisory-tracker.com and to any unfamiliar /api/v1/telemetry endpoint; audit the org's Sentry projects for forged issues containing markdown resolution sections.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          GrandparentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f

author: Clankerusecase

detection:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
