npm/node install-time process beaconing to webhook.site, sfrclak.com or 142.11.206.73 AICommand & Control High
Hunts the exfil-leg of the article's named campaigns where an install-time lifecycle script beacons to webhook.site (canary inbox) or to known campaign infrastructure (sfrclak.com, 142.11.206.73) to ship harvested tokens. High-fidelity because legitimate npm packages do not POST credentials to webhook.site mid-install. Rationale: Hard IOCs from the article: domain sfrclak.com, IP 142.11.206.73, and webhook.site as the canary inbox commonly used by the Shai-Hulud lineage. Binding the egress to an npm/node/yarn/pnpm/bun process gates out personal webhook.site usage by developers in unrelated tooling. Sentinel query unioned across ImDnsActivity / ImNetworkSession / ImProcessCreate — no DeviceName references on tables that don't carry it.
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer testing their own webhook.site inbox via a quick node REPL or `curl`-via-`npm exec` — match on InitiatingProcessParentFileName==cmd/powershell rather than npm-lifecycle parent
  • Legitimate package using webhook.site as a documented test endpoint (rare, vet by package name)
  • An internal reverse-proxy that legitimately resolves to 142.11.206.73 (verify with NetOps before suppressing)
  • Pre-existing Aikido / SafeChain telemetry callbacks if a competitor product uses webhook.site for ack
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("safe-chain","aikido") and RemoteUrl has "webhook.site")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceProcessEvents on the same DeviceId 5 minutes before the network event to identify the originating `npm install` and the specific package directory under node_modules (the script body usually drops in postinstall.js / telemetry.js / index.js of the rogue package). 2) Contain: yank network from the host, revoke npm publish tokens + GitHub PATs + cloud SSO sessions for the developer, block sfrclak.com + 142.11.206.73 at perimeter, and add the package@version to your internal denylist. 3) Hunt: tstats 30 days back for any other host that contacted those same IOCs from a node-family parent; check GitHub for new repos named like `Shai-Hulud-*` or with the user's PAT scoped to public-repo create.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","sfrclak.com"]);
let SuspectIPs = dynamic(["142.11.206.73"]);
let InstallProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (InstallProcs)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (InstallProcs)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install","preinstall","postinstall")
| where RemoteUrl has_any (SuspectDomains)
   or RemoteIP in (SuspectIPs)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","sfrclak.com"]);
let SuspectIPs = dynamic(["142.11.206.73"]);
let InstallProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe"]);
let DnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (SuspectDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, SrcHost = SrcHostname, SrcIp = SrcIpAddr,
              Indicator = DnsQuery, Source = "DNS";
let NetHits = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstIpAddr in (SuspectIPs) or DstHostname has_any (SuspectDomains) or Url has_any (SuspectDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, SrcHost = SrcHostname, SrcIp = SrcIpAddr,
              Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url), Source = "Net";
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (InstallProcs) or ParentProcessName has_any (InstallProcs)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (SuspectDomains) or ActingProcessCommandLine has "142.11.206.73"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, SrcHost = DvcHostname, SrcIp = DvcIpAddr,
              Indicator = ActingProcessCommandLine, Source = "Proc";
union DnsHits, NetHits, ProcHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Implicit node-gyp rebuild from binding.gyp spawns suspicious build child AIInstallation Medium
Targets the new attack surface the article highlights — packages without any declared scripts that still execute code via an implicit `node-gyp rebuild` triggered by binding.gyp. Detects node-gyp invoking compilers / interpreters / network tools that don't belong in a native-module build. Rationale: The article specifically names the binding.gyp / implicit `node-gyp rebuild` path as a covert execution channel that v12 will block. Genuine native-module builds spawn compilers (cl.exe, link.exe, gyp.exe) — they should never need powershell/curl/certutil. Child set is the standard LOLBin/network-downloader allowlist.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Native module that legitimately shells out to powershell to detect Windows SDK / Visual Studio paths (some node-canvas / node-sass forks)
  • node-pre-gyp using curl/wget to fetch prebuilt binaries (legitimate but article-relevant — review)
  • Developer environments running `npm install` with --verbose where parent-cmdline chaining produces false parents
  • CI nodes that wrap node-gyp in a shell script for cross-compilation
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-pre-gyp","prebuild-install") and FileName =~ "curl.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "github.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the package owning the binding.gyp from the working directory in InitiatingProcessFolderPath (look under node_modules/<pkg>/binding.gyp), pull the SHA256 of the child binary, and dump the script body if the child is a scripting host. 2) Contain: quarantine the package version, remove from internal mirror/proxy, kick CI jobs that pulled it in the last 24h, and rotate any developer-tier secrets present in the build environment. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceFileEvents for files written under %TEMP%/%APPDATA%/.npm/_cacache during the build window, and DeviceNetworkEvents for non-prebuilt-binary URLs (anything outside github.com/<pkg> releases or the org's artifact registry).
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let UnexpectedChildren = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node-gyp"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "binding.gyp"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "npm install"
      and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node-gyp rebuild"
| where FileName in~ (UnexpectedChildren)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let UnexpectedChildren = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","binding.gyp","node-gyp rebuild")
| where ActingProcessName has_any (UnexpectedChildren)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: node-gyp implicit rebuild spawns scripting/networking child
id: 9c1a8d54-2b7e-4c5f-a9d1-04e2f7a8c133
description: A node-gyp build (often triggered implicitly during npm install by a package's binding.gyp) spawns a shell, scripting host, or network downloader — the covert execution path the npm v12 allowlist is designed to close.
references:

author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

  product: windows
detection:
  parent_selection:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentCommandLine:(*node-gyp* OR *binding.gyp* OR *"node-gyp rebuild"*) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe)

| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|curl|wget|certutil|bitsadmin|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32)\.exe$/i

npm install-time process reads .npmrc, SSH key, or cloud-credential file AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the credential-harvesting step of Nx s1ngularity / Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud — install-time scripts read .npmrc (auth tokens), ~/.ssh/id_* (SSH keys), and AWS/GitHub credential files. The article lists these exact artefacts as what the postinstall payloads scrape. Rationale: Article enumerates exactly these victim artefacts — 'scans for tokens, SSH keys, and other goodies', and Nx s1ngularity is called out specifically as harvesting GitHub tokens, npm credentials, SSH keys, and crypto wallets. Filtering on install-time parent + ≥2 credential-file hits in one process strips out IDE indexing noise while keeping the harvester pattern.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate npm CLI reading user's own .npmrc during publish/login (filter on npm-cli.js parent + 'npm publish' command line)
  • VS Code remote-ssh extension's node host enumerating ~/.ssh during workspace open
  • yarn classic touching .npmrc to migrate auth tokens on first install
  • Developer running aws-sdk-node example that reads ~/.aws/credentials intentionally
Suppression filter
| where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm publish","npm login","npm whoami") and TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the originating process tree and the package directory under node_modules to identify the rogue package; capture the script body before the file deletes itself (article notes the harvesters self-delete). 2) Contain: immediately rotate every credential the process touched — npm tokens via `npm token revoke`, GitHub PATs in GH settings, AWS keys via IAM, force-push SSH key re-keying. Quarantine the host. 3) Hunt: search GitHub audit logs for new public repos created by the user's PAT in the last 24h (Shai-Hulud uploads stolen creds to public repos), pivot to other hosts that installed the same package@version via your internal registry logs.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let InstallProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe"]);
let CredPaths = dynamic([".npmrc",".ssh\\id_rsa",".ssh\\id_ed25519",".ssh\\id_ecdsa",".aws\\credentials",".config\\gh\\hosts.yml",".gitconfig",".netrc","npm\\.npmrc"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileRead","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (InstallProcs)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (InstallProcs)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install","postinstall","preinstall")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize CredFiles = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName), 25),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count()
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
               InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where Hits >= 2 or array_length(CredFiles) >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let InstallProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe"]);
let CredPaths = dynamic([".npmrc",".ssh/id_rsa",".ssh/id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ecdsa",".aws/credentials",".config/gh/hosts.yml",".gitconfig",".netrc"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileModified","FileRead")
| where ActingProcessName has_any (InstallProcs)
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install","postinstall","preinstall")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths) or TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize CredFiles = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count()
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where Hits >= 2 or array_length(CredFiles) >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\bun.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\.npmrc* OR *\\.ssh\\id_rsa* OR *\\.ssh\\id_ed25519* OR *\\.aws\\credentials* OR *\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml* OR *\\.netrc*)
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten) ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|npx|yarn|pnpm|bun)\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\\\\\.npmrc|\\\\\\.ssh\\\\id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|\\\\\\.config\\\\gh\\\\hosts\\.yml|\\\\\\.netrc)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| count > 1

npm lifecycle script harvests secrets via TruffleHog or chains to GitHub API AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Shai-Hulud-specific behaviour the article describes — install-time scripts that download and run TruffleHog to scrape secrets, then chain to a GitHub API call (api.github.com) to publish stolen credentials to a public repo. High-fidelity because TruffleHog under an npm-install parent is otherwise zero. Rationale: Article names both 'ran TruffleHog to scrape secrets' and 'dumped them into public GitHub repos' as the Shai-Hulud signature. Public-repo creation via api.github.com/user/repos or `gh repo create --public` under a node-family parent has no benign workflow we've ever seen.
ATT&CKT1552 T1567.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A security-team CI job that legitimately runs TruffleHog as a pre-commit/post-install secret-scan in a sanctioned pipeline — tag those hosts and exclude
  • Developer running `npm exec gh-action-secrets-scan` in a sanctioned tool
  • A package that bundles trufflehog as a transitive dependency for its OWN secret-scanning feature (rare; vet by package name)
  • Internal devx tool that auto-creates public template repos on first install
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sec-ci","appsec-runner") and ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the originating npm-install command and rogue package version from process-tree context, snapshot the working directory before self-deletion, and record the SHA256 of any trufflehog.exe / gitleaks.exe binary dropped. 2) Contain: revoke all developer secrets in scope (GitHub PAT, npm tokens, SSH, AWS, cloud SSO), force-delete any public repo created by the user's PAT in the last 24h via `gh repo delete --yes`, quarantine the host, denylist the package version. 3) Hunt: query GitHub audit logs for `repo.create` + `repo.public` events by the user in 48h window, search EmailEvents for any maintainer-targeted phishing in the prior week (article notes the worm starts with a maintainer phish), and pivot to other internal hosts that pulled the package via internal-registry access logs.
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let InstallParents = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe"]);
let ScraperIndicators = dynamic(["trufflehog","gitleaks","detect-secrets","api.github.com/user/repos","gh repo create --public","Shai-Hulud"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (InstallParents)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (InstallParents)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("postinstall","preinstall","npm install","npm ci")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (ScraperIndicators)
   or FileName has_any ("trufflehog.exe","gitleaks.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let InstallParents = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe"]);
let ScraperIndicators = dynamic(["trufflehog","gitleaks","detect-secrets","api.github.com/user/repos","gh repo create --public","Shai-Hulud"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (InstallParents)
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("postinstall","preinstall","npm install","npm ci")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (ScraperIndicators)
   or ActingProcessName has_any ("trufflehog.exe","gitleaks.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm lifecycle script invokes TruffleHog or GitHub-repo-create CLI
id: 2f3b6a18-4d8c-49aa-bd0f-7a3e1c8b2d44
description: A node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun install-time process invokes TruffleHog/Gitleaks or chains to api.github.com/user/repos — the Shai-Hulud worm's exact post-harvest publication step.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1552
  - attack.t1567.001
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent_selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
  child_selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'trufflehog'
      - 'gitleaks'
      - 'detect-secrets'
      - 'api.github.com/user/repos'
      - 'gh repo create --public'
      - 'Shai-Hulud'
  condition: parent_selection and child_selection
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\bun.exe) @CommandLine:(*trufflehog* OR *TruffleHog* OR *gitleaks* OR *"api.github.com/user/repos"* OR *"gh repo create --public"* OR *Shai-Hulud*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(node|npm|npx|yarn|pnpm|bun)\.exe$/i
| (CommandLine=/trufflehog/i OR CommandLine=/gitleaks/i OR CommandLine=/detect-secrets/i OR CommandLine=/api\.github\.com\/user\/repos/i OR CommandLine=/gh\s+repo\s+create\s+--public/i OR CommandLine=/Shai-Hulud/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*postinstall*","*preinstall*")) AND (Processes.process IN ("*trufflehog*","*gitleaks*","*detect-secrets*","*api.github.com/user/repos*","*gh repo create --public*","*git push*https://*@github.com*")) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*postinstall*","*preinstall*")) AND (Processes.process IN ("*trufflehog*","*gitleaks*","*detect-secrets*","*api.github.com/user/repos*","*gh repo create --public*","*git push*https://*@github.com*")) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High
Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.
ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Unauthenticated POST to /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 (CVE-2026-48039) AIDelivery High
Hunts inbound HTTP POST requests to the Meta Ads MCP `/mcp` Streamable HTTP endpoint that arrive without an Authorization header (or Pipeboard token cookie) yet receive an HTTP 200 response. Per the advisory, `AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch()` falls through to `call_next` when no auth tokens are present, allowing any network-reachable caller to invoke MCP tools. Rationale: Anchored on the article's PoC: POST /mcp on TCP 8080 with no auth headers returning HTTP 200. Joins network telemetry to host-side process inventory of meta_ads_mcp to filter out arbitrary port-8080 scans. Cross-checked the streamable HTTP transport setup against the project's STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md and the PyPI release page. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/ • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal load balancer or k8s liveness/readiness probes to /mcp returning 200
  • Authenticated Pipeboard SaaS clients reaching the server from CDN egress IPs
  • Internal red-team or vuln-scanner sweeps (Nuclei, Burp, Nessus) hitting /mcp
  • Misclassified WAN→DMZ traffic when X-Forwarded-For not parsed and client_ip shows the proxy
  • Reverse-proxied legitimate traffic where Authorization header is stripped before reaching the listener
Suppression filter
and not (SrcIpAddr in (<load_balancer_ips>, <pipeboard_egress_ips>)) and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("kube-probe", "ELB-HealthChecker", "GoogleHC")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on SrcIpAddr — pull a 10-minute window of all requests, look for `tools/call` JSON-RPC payloads (especially `get_ad_accounts`, `get_campaigns`, `get_ads`) and check the response body for `request_url` containing `access_token=`. WHOIS / threat-intel the source IP. 2) Contain: rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN at developers.facebook.com immediately, redeploy the container with the token revoked, and either firewall TCP 8080 to internal CIDRs only or front the server with a reverse proxy that enforces auth. Upgrade meta-ads-mcp past v1.0.108. 3) Hunt: query graph.facebook.com outbound for the previous 30 days for any URL containing `access_token=` (see UC: Graph API URL leak), and review Meta Business Manager audit log for ad-account activity from unfamiliar IPs in the same window.
// CVE-2026-48039 — inbound to vulnerable meta-ads-mcp listener on 8080
let MCPHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
    | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 8080
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP))
| join kind=inner MCPHosts on DeviceId
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DistinctSrc = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, RemoteIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by FirstSeen desc
// CVE-2026-48039 exploitation — unauthenticated POST /mcp on 8080
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where DstPortNumber == 8080
| where Url has "/mcp"
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr) and not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization) or HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization == ""
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctURLs = dcount(Url), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr
| order by FirstSeen desc

description: Detects HTTP POST requests to the Meta Ads MCP /mcp Streamable HTTP endpoint on TCP 8080 returning HTTP 200, which under CVE-2026-48039 indicates successful unauthenticated tool execution.

author: SOC Detection Engineering

  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1133

  category: webserver
detection:

    cs-method: POST
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/mcp'
    s-port: 8080
    sc-status: 200
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Internal load balancer health checks (filter by source CIDR)
  - Authenticated Pipeboard / MCP clients (filter on presence of Authorization header)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:envoy OR source:traefik) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*/mcp* @network.destination.port:8080 @http.status_code:[200 TO 299] -CIDR(@network.client.ip, 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 LocalPort=8080 ConnectionDirection=1
| ContextImageFileName=/(python|python3|uvicorn|gunicorn|docker|containerd-shim)/i
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("127.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)

Meta Graph API request with access_token in URL query string (CVE-2026-48039 leak signature) AICommand & Control High
Detects HTTPS requests to graph.facebook.com whose URL contains the `access_token=` query parameter — the exact leak signature for CVE-2026-48039 where the vulnerable `make_api_request()` in `api.py:136` appends the operator token to the URL and surfaces it in the JSON-RPC error response. Same query also catches an external attacker reusing a stolen META_ACCESS_TOKEN from a corporate-network host via curl/python/PowerShell. Rationale: Anchored on the article's PoC response payload: `request_url` containing `https://graph.facebook.com/v24.0/me/adaccounts?...&access_token=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789`. Tokens in URL query strings (vs Authorization headers) is itself a Meta-Graph-SDK anti-pattern, so even outside this CVE the hit is high-fidelity. Captures a token preview for triage without storing the whole credential. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/
ATT&CKT1528 T1041 T1552.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate marketing-team scripts using the old Meta Graph SDK that still passes `access_token` in URL
  • Internal Meta Ads dashboards built before the Bearer-header migration
  • Backup/export tooling using legacy Facebook API v2.x patterns
  • Penetration tester replaying captured traffic
  • Browser-based Meta Business Manager flows where the SDK falls back to query-string auth for older browsers
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("FacebookAdsSdk.exe","meta-ads-export.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--legacy-auth" and InitiatingProcessAccountName has "svc-marketing")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on TokenPreview — group all hits by token prefix to see whether one leaked credential is being reused. Cross-reference SrcIpAddr/DeviceName against UC-1 hits (the /mcp inbound) to tie source → leaked credential. 2) Contain: revoke the leaked META_ACCESS_TOKEN via Meta Business Manager → Business Settings → System Users → Generate New Token, then redeploy meta-ads-mcp with the rotated token and apply the upstream patch (v1.0.109+ when available, or downstream patch removing access_token from URL). 3) Hunt: check Meta Business audit log for ad-account changes (campaign creation, ad spend modifications, page admin additions) in the time window of the leak; query for the same TokenPreview prefix in the past 90 days; review any other systems sharing the META_ACCESS_TOKEN env var.
// CVE-2026-48039 token leak — Graph API URL carrying access_token
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.facebook.com"
| where RemoteUrl has "access_token="
| extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, RemoteUrl)
| extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, RemoteUrl)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, GraphPath, TokenPreview
| union (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "graph.facebook.com" and ProcessCommandLine has "access_token="
    | where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","python3.exe")
    | extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, RemoteIP=tostring(dynamic(null)), RemotePort=toint(0), RemoteUrl=ProcessCommandLine, GraphPath, TokenPreview
)
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 leak — proxy / ASIM web session carrying access_token to graph.facebook.com
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpHostName =~ "graph.facebook.com" or Url has "graph.facebook.com"
| where Url has "access_token="
| extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, Url)
| extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, Url)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname=HttpHostName, Url, GraphPath, TokenPreview, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctTokens = dcount(TokenPreview), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstHostname
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Meta Graph API URL Carrying access_token Query Parameter (CVE-2026-48039 Leak)
id: 8f3b7e55-9d3c-5a0f-cf06-2d4b1f6e5c3a
description: Detects HTTPS requests to graph.facebook.com whose URL contains access_token= in the query string — the leak signature for CVE-2026-48039 (meta-ads-mcp) and credential reuse post-theft.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_host:
    cs-host|contains: 'graph.facebook.com'
  selection_token:
    cs-uri-query|contains: 'access_token='
  condition: selection_host and selection_token
falsepositives:
  - Legacy Meta Graph SDKs that pass access_token via query string instead of Authorization header (should be modernised regardless)
level: high
(@http.url_details.host:graph.facebook.com OR @http.url:*graph.facebook.com*) (@http.url:*access_token=* OR @http.url_details.queryString.access_token:*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^graph\.facebook\.com$/i

| join({
    #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
    | CommandLine=/graph\.facebook\.com/i
    | CommandLine=/access_token=/i
    | TokenPreview := regex("access_token=(?<TokenPreview>[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,12})", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
  }, field=[aid, ContextProcessId=TargetProcessId])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, TokenPreview], function=count(as=hits))

Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp installation inventory (CVE-2026-48039) on managed hosts AIReconnaissance High
Inventory-style hunt that surfaces every managed host running meta-ads-mcp (any version), then flags installations at v1.0.108 or earlier as vulnerable to CVE-2026-48039. Pivots on both pip-installed and Docker-deployed instances since the project ships both ways. Rationale: Article specifies the affected version range (`≤ 1.0.101` confirmed, `1.0.102–1.0.105` lacking git tags, package metadata listing `vuln <= 1.0.108`). Pinning to `^1\.0\.(\d|[1-9]\d|10[0-8])$` matches every published vulnerable version while excluding 1.0.109+. Cross-checked against PyPI release listing. Cross-checked against: • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/ • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1518
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer laptops running the package against a sandbox Meta Ads test account (not actually exposed)
  • CI/CD runners installing meta-ads-mcp ephemerally for integration tests
  • Versions strings appearing in pip download cache filenames without an actual running listener
  • Patched 1.0.109+ instances whose container tag still carries an old version label
  • Vendored copies in monorepos where the version string in path doesn't reflect the deployed binary
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each host flagged YES, confirm a live listener exists via `netstat -an | findstr 8080` (or `ss -tlnp` on Linux) and check whether the listener is bound to 0.0.0.0 vs 127.0.0.1. 2) Contain: upgrade vulnerable hosts to meta-ads-mcp v1.0.109+ (once available), or apply the upstream remediation from the advisory (return 401 in `AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch()` and strip `access_token` from `request_url`). In the interim, firewall TCP 8080 to internal CIDRs only. 3) Hunt: pivot from each vulnerable host into UC-1 (any inbound /mcp POSTs) and UC-2 (any outbound graph.facebook.com URL carrying access_token) over the past 30 days to assess pre-detection exposure.
// CVE-2026-48039 — inventory hunt for meta-ads-mcp installations
let ProcessSightings = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
    | extend FullCmd = strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, " || ", ProcessCommandLine)

meta-ads-mcp Streamable HTTP listener bound to non-loopback interface AIWeaponization High
Hunts processes invoking meta-ads-mcp where the HTTP transport is bound to a public/non-loopback interface (0.0.0.0 or a routable IP) rather than 127.0.0.1, and Docker `docker run -p` mappings that publish TCP 8080 outside the host loopback. Per the article's own PoC the safe binding is `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080`; anything else exposes the unauthenticated /mcp endpoint to the network. Rationale: The article's PoC uses `docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 ...` — i.e. the safe loopback binding. The dangerous variants (`-p 8080:8080`, `-p 0.0.0.0:8080:8080`, `--host 0.0.0.0`) publish the unauthenticated /mcp endpoint to every network reachable to the host. Detecting the exposed binding lets a SOC reduce the attack surface BEFORE inbound traffic arrives. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md
ATT&CKT1133 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Intentional internal-only deployment behind a network firewall/segment where 0.0.0.0 binding is fine because the host is unreachable from the internet
  • Kubernetes pods using 0.0.0.0 binding inside the pod network (intentional, fronted by ClusterIP Service)
  • Developer staging containers on isolated bridge networks
  • Reverse-proxy patterns where Nginx fronts the listener on 8080 and enforces auth upstream
  • Operators using `--host ::` (IPv6 wildcard) instead of 0.0.0.0 — this signature misses that case
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("kubelet.exe","kubelet") and not (ParentProcessName has_any ("containerd-shim","docker-proxy") and DvcHostname has "k8s-internal")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the listener is actually reachable from outside the host by attempting a connection from a non-trusted network to the host's public/RFC1918 IP on TCP 8080. Look for an upstream reverse proxy enforcing auth. 2) Contain: stop the container/process, restart with `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080` (or in Kubernetes, switch the Service from LoadBalancer/NodePort to ClusterIP). Apply network policy/security-group rule blocking 8080 ingress. 3) Hunt: if the listener was reachable, query UC-1 (inbound /mcp POSTs) and UC-2 (graph.facebook.com URL with access_token) for the host's public IP and any private interfaces, going back to the host's first sighting of the vulnerable binary.
// CVE-2026-48039 — meta-ads-mcp listener exposed beyond loopback
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, " || ", ProcessCommandLine)
| where FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(--host\s+0\.0\.0\.0|--host\s+\*|0\.0\.0\.0:8080|-p\s+8080:8080(\s|$)|-p\s+0\.0\.0\.0:8080:|--publish[= ]0\.0\.0\.0:8080)"
| where not(FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(127\.0\.0\.1:8080:8080|-p\s+127\.0\.0\.1:8080|--host\s+127\.0\.0\.1|--host\s+localhost)")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — meta-ads-mcp exposed listener via process create
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(coalesce(ParentProcessCommandLine,""), " || ", coalesce(ActingProcessCommandLine,""))
| where FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(--host\s+0\.0\.0\.0|--host\s+\*|0\.0\.0\.0:8080|-p\s+8080:8080(\s|$)|-p\s+0\.0\.0\.0:8080:|--publish[= ]0\.0\.0\.0:8080)"
| where not(FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(127\.0\.0\.1:8080:8080|-p\s+127\.0\.0\.1:8080|--host\s+127\.0\.0\.1|--host\s+localhost)")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@CommandLine:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp*) OR @process.command_line:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp*)) (@CommandLine:(*"--host 0.0.0.0"* OR *"-p 8080:8080"* OR *"0.0.0.0:8080"*) OR @process.command_line:(*"--host 0.0.0.0"* OR *"-p 8080:8080"* OR *"0.0.0.0:8080"*)) -@CommandLine:(*"127.0.0.1:8080:8080"* OR *"--host 127.0.0.1"* OR *"--host localhost"*) -@process.command_line:(*"127.0.0.1:8080:8080"* OR *"--host 127.0.0.1"* OR *"--host localhost"*)

CVE-2026-48039 PoC artifact execution (meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 image, FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO env) AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact PoC artifacts published with the advisory: a Docker image tagged `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001`, the `META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789` env-var literal, and a `poc.py` exploit script run from an interactive shell. Hits indicate an analyst, red-teamer, or attacker actively rehearsing the PoC inside the environment. Rationale: PoC strings are pulled verbatim from the article — the docker invocation `docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -e META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789 meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` and the `python3 poc.py` runner. The image tag `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` and the FAKE_TOKEN literal have no legitimate use outside reproducing the advisory PoC, so hits should be treated as either (a) authorised purple-team activity or (b) attacker rehearsal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.006 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security team rehearsing the PoC in a sandbox — should be allowlisted by host or by tagged session
  • Vulnerability-management vendors running their own validation harness against staging
  • Security-research blog post readers copy-pasting the PoC on their workstation
  • Generic poc.py filenames unrelated to this CVE (filtered out by the meta-ads-mcp / graph.facebook.com co-occurrence requirement)
  • Container image-scanning pipelines pulling the image for SBOM analysis (filter by parent image-scanner process)
Suppression filter
and DvcHostname !startswith "redteam-" and DvcHostname !startswith "vulnscan-" and ActorUsername !in~ ("svc-purpleteam","redteam-runner")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the host belongs to the security team's red-team / vuln-research fleet (check asset tags). If unknown, capture the full process tree and any inbound/outbound network connections from the same host in a ±15-minute window. 2) Contain: isolate the host via EDR network containment if it's NOT a sanctioned research host. Snapshot disk + memory for forensics. Revoke any Meta access tokens that share the host's environment (in case real tokens were also tested). 3) Hunt: pivot on the operator account that ran the PoC — query for any access to internal meta-ads-mcp servers (UC-1 inbound /mcp), graph.facebook.com URLs carrying access_token (UC-2), and lateral movement from this host in the same session; review git history on the host for clones of pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp.
// CVE-2026-48039 — PoC artefacts (docker image, fake token literal, poc.py exploit)
let ProcMatches = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "meta-ads-mcp-vuln001"
         or ProcessCommandLine has "FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO"
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "meta-ads-mcp-vuln001"
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO"
         or (ProcessCommandLine has "poc.py" and (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","graph.facebook.com","/mcp","tools/call","get_ad_accounts")))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "process";
let FileMatches = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "poc.py"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","code.exe","pwsh.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","explorer.exe","curl.exe","git.exe")
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr","CVE-2026-48039")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine = "", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "file";
union ProcMatches, FileMatches
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — PoC artefacts via ASIM
let ProcMatches = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
         or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
         or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "poc.py" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","graph.facebook.com","/mcp","tools/call","get_ad_accounts"))
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="process";
let FileMatches = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "poc.py"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","code","pwsh","powershell","bash","git","curl")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, Source="file";
union ProcMatches, FileMatches
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Miasma supply-chain worm leaked repo clone, install or fetch · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Cybersecurity Stars Awards 2026: Winners Announced Across 95 Categories
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Miasma worm GitHub commit-search C2 magic strings on command line or script · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Miasma worm GitHub commit-search C2 magic strings on command line or script AICommand & Control High
Hunts for the three hard-coded GitHub commit-search query strings the Miasma supply-chain worm uses as its three independent C2 channels (PAT discovery, JavaScript payload delivery, Python payload delivery). These strings have zero legitimate business presence and are the highest-fidelity Miasma indicator available. Rationale: The three strings 'DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom', 'TheBeautifulSandsOfTime' and 'firedalazer' are the hard-coded GitHub commit-search queries each Miasma C2 channel uses (PAT discovery, JS payload, Python payload). They are confirmed by SafeDep's analysis, BleepingComputer's report, and a parallel TheHackerNews write-up. Zero legitimate business processes contain these tokens. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-supply-chain-attack-compromises.html • https://cloudsmith.com/blog/miasma-worms-path-of-destruction • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/06/09/miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit-goes-public-on-github/5253074
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.007 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst running these strings through their own grep/search tooling for hunting
  • SOC engineer pasting the IOCs into a script or note file
  • Security researcher cloning or reading SafeDep / Cloudsmith write-ups in a developer IDE that logs URL paths
  • Sandbox / detonation environment intentionally executing a Miasma sample for analysis
  • Automation that ingests OSS-supply-chain advisories and writes IOCs to a database column
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("misp.exe","opencti.exe") and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\sandbox\\","\\detonation\\","\\analyst-tools\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the process that emitted the string is not an analyst hunting tool, a CTI ingestion script, or a known sandbox. Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and parent chain; if the string was in a network URL, identify what process issued the GET against api.github.com/search/commits. 2) Contain: if the originating process is a node/python/git/curl invocation on a developer machine or CI runner, isolate the host from network, revoke any GitHub PATs and SSH keys cached on it, and rotate npm/PyPI/RubyGems publish tokens and JFrog Artifactory credentials owned by that user. 3) Hunt: search 30d for the same three strings org-wide; pivot on the parent process and SHA256 to find sibling executions; review the developer's git push history for npm/PyPI/RubyGems package versions published in the last 7d for unexpected new releases or postinstall scripts.
let MiasmaC2 = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSandsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, Source = "Process";
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","github.com")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName = InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256, Source = strcat("Net:", RemoteUrl);
union ProcHits, NetHits
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaC2 = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSandsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
let From4688 = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source = "4688";
let FromAsim = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (MiasmaC2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName = ActingProcessName, Source = "ASIM";
union From4688, FromAsim
| where Account !endswith "$"
| order by TimeGenerated desc
